But when it is introduced without a comparison, the majority may be the opposite of that, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He preferred us over many of His believing servants﴾. So his statement that the attribute of multitude, if made restrictive, and so on, is a statement that did not proceed from firm ground. For this reason, the author of al-Taqrib said: it is possible to indicate that it is less preferred.

This is the matter. Furthermore, the question of preference is a matter of difference among the People of the Sunna. Some of them went to the preference of the angels, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and the choice of al-Zajjaj as related by al-Wahidi in al-Basit. Others made a distinction and said: The messengers from among the human are superior absolutely; then the messengers from among the angels are superior to all others, human and angelic; then the generality of the angels over the generality of the human. This is what the followers of Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, hold, as do many of the Shafi'is and the Ash'aris. Others generalized the preference of the perfected ones (al-kummal) of the human race, whether prophets or saints. Others preferred the Karubiyyun (the cherubim) among the angels absolutely, then the messengers from among the human, then the perfected ones among them, then the generality of the angels over the generality of the human.

This is what al-Imam al-Razi held, and the words of al-Ghazali in many places in his books indicate it. From this it is known that the unqualified statement that the People of the Sunna prefer the human over the angel is not as it should be. This matter and the matter of the preference of the Imams are not among those for which one who goes to either extreme is labeled an innovator, according to what is in al-Kashf, since it does not return to a principle of belief and does not rest on a definitive text, after being free from criticism and from anything that harms the reverence due in both matters. But the well-known position on the matter of the preference of the Imams is that holding a view contrary to what the position of the People of the Sunna has settled upon is innovation (bid'a). Whoever is just says what is in al-Kashf. So the ravings of al-Zamakhshari against one who opposes him are pure ignorance, if he was not at that extreme. How much more so when he has reached in it the utmost of foolishness and the ultimate of vulgarity! He will see the recompense for that.

[Page 120]

﴿The Day We shall call every people with their leader﴾: this begins an explanation of the differences in the states of the children of Adam in the Hereafter, after the description of their states in this world. "Yawm" (day) is the object of a deleted verb, meaning: "Remember the Day when We call..." and so on.

Ibn 'Atiyya and others permitted it to be an adverb (zarf) of a verb indicated by "﴿they will not be wronged﴾". However, it was not made an adverb of that verb, on the basis that the fa' (the conditional particle "fa" in what follows) does not allow what comes after it to govern what comes before it, even if it is an adverb. It was also permitted for it to be the subject (mubtada') of a sentence, in which case it is indeclinable (mabni) because it is attached to a non-declinable clause, and the predicate (khabar) is the clause "﴿whoever is given﴾" and so on, with a pronoun to link it to the subject, which is to be supposed in it. In this there is the point that what is divided into declinable and indeclinable is the noun, not the verb, and what is here is a present-tense verb. Moreover, the indeclinability of time-nouns attached to a clause is, according to the view of the Kufans and the Basrans, one of their two components, and they do not permit that. Despite this, it is a strained interpretation.

It was also permitted for it to be an adverb of "﴿We have favoured them﴾". He said: The favouring of mankind over the rest of the animals on the Day of Resurrection is "clear." Some grammarians also held this view, except that he said: "We favoured them with reward." In this there is the point: what favour is there for mankind on that Day, when the disbelievers among them are the basest of all creatures? Unless it is said that favouring the species suffices by favouring some of its individuals. Do you not see that the men are better than the women, although among women there are some who are better than some men by many degrees? Also, if the favour meant is by reward, it is not correct to exclude the angels, because the human species is rewarded while the angels, peace be upon them, are not rewarded, as is established in its proper place. Furthermore, the jinn share with them in reward, since their believers are rewarded as humans are, according to some. It was said that their reward is less than the reward of humans, because they do not see God, Exalted is He, in Paradise, according to those who say that God, Exalted is He, is seen there. So humans are favoured over them in reward from this aspect.

It was said that the adverb is "﴿they will read﴾" or what indicates it. In this there is the point that they do not read their book at the time of the calling. It has been answered that what is meant by "the Day they are called" is a long period of time, which is the last day in which what will happen will happen. Making it an adverb of what is mentioned leaves the matter of the fa'.

Al-Farra' said: it is an adverb of a deleted "﴿We will raise you up﴾". It was said: it is an adverb of "﴿they will respond﴾". It was said: it is a substitute (badal) for "﴿the Day He calls you﴾". It was said: the governing element in it is what is indicated by His, Exalted is He, saying "﴿When is it?﴾". These views are extremely weak, and the nearest and strongest of the views is what we mentioned first.

The "imam" is the one followed and imitated, whether rational or otherwise. The prepositional phrase is connected to "We call"; that is: We call every people from among the children of Adam, those whom We honoured in this world with what We honoured them, and what is joined to it, by the one they followed, whether a prophet, or a leader in religion, or a book, or a religion. So it is said: "O followers of so-and-so! O people of such-and-such a religion, or of such-and-such a book!"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Ali, may God honour his face, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said concerning the verse: "Every people will be called with the imam of their time, the Book of their Lord and the Sunnah of their Prophet."

[Page 121]

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Imam" means the imam of guidance and the imam of misguidance.

Ibn Jarir narrated through al-'Awfi from him, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "With their imam" means with the book of their deeds. Then it will be said: "O companions of the book of good! O companions of the book of evil!" This was also narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' and al-Hasan.

It was read: "bi-kitabihim" (with their book). Perhaps the reason that this is their imam is that they follow what it judges, whether Paradise or Hell. Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: it is their book which was revealed to them.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib in his History narrated from Anas that he said: it is their prophet who was sent to them.

Ibn 'Atiyya, like others, chose that "imam" be general, in accordance with what has been mentioned in the reports. It was also said: what is meant are the powers which drive them to their beliefs and actions, such as the theoretical and practical faculty, the irascible and the appetitive faculties, whether the appetite is for money, property, or rank and leadership. They were called "imam" because they follow them. This view, although not transmitted, is very far-fetched, so one does not follow its speaker, even if he is an imam.

In al-Kashshaf it is stated that among the strange interpretations is that "imam" is the plural of "umm" (mother), like "khuff" and "khifaf" (sock/socks), and that people will be called on the Day of Resurrection by their mothers. The wisdom in calling them by their mothers rather than their fathers is to honour the right of 'Isa, peace be upon him, the nobility of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and so as not to disgrace the children of fornication. "How I wonder which of the two is more wonderful: the soundness of his interpretation or the splendour of his wisdom." End of quotation. This is also narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b.

The reason this is not accepted, according to what is in al-Kashf, is: first, that "imam" as the plural of "umm" is not common; what is known is "ummahat" (mothers). Second, that honouring the right of 'Isa, peace be upon him, by distinguishing him through being called by his mother, since his creation without a father was a dignity for him and not a diminution, so that it would be compensated by saying that people share with him in being connected to mothers; and displaying the nobility of al-Hasanayn is more complete without that, for their father is better than their mother, and the People of the House are like a closed ring. As for the disgrace of the children of fornication, there is no disgrace except for the mothers, and it is already there whether others are called by their mothers or by their fathers, and they bear no sin in that, so that disgrace would follow from it. End of quotation.

As for the statement that this plural is not common, it is clear. As for the criticism of the wisdom, it has been responded to: its essence is that if all people were called by their fathers and 'Isa, peace be upon him, were called by his mother, that might suggest a deficiency. So the honour of his, peace be upon him, was respected, and everyone was called by their mothers. Likewise the honour of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them both, was respected, because this shows their lineage from the Messenger of God ﷺ, even if their lineage is traced to their father, may God honour his face, this would not be understood, even though he is himself, may God be pleased with him. Also in that there is a covering over the creation, so that the children of fornication are not disgraced. For if people were called by their fathers and they were called by their mothers, it would be known that they have no lineage to fathers by whom they could be called, and that would be a stigma for them. If they were called by fathers, they would not be known by them in this world, even if they are not legally attributed to them; it would be so. On this basis, what is in al-Kashf falls away.

In my view, whoever says this hardly says it without relying on a report, because it contradicts what comes to the minds of people, with differing levels of understanding, and its wisdom can hardly be free of flaw. "The perfumer cannot repair what time has spoiled."

Perhaps the report, if it is not sound, is contradicted by what we have already mentioned, which is not far from the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "You will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and the names of your fathers, so make your names good."

And God knows best. What has been mentioned about the prepositional phrase being connected to what is before it is the apparent view, to which the majority adhere. It was permitted that it be connected to a deleted element that serves as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning "accompanied by their imam." Then the caller is either God, Mighty and Majestic, or the angel, which is what the reports suggest. So the attribution of the verb to Him, Exalted is He, is metaphorical.

Mujahid read "yad'u" with the letter ya' (third person), meaning: God, Exalted is He, or the angel calls. Al-Hasan, in one transmission, read "yud'a" in the passive form, with "kull" (every) as the deputy of the subject. In another transmission, "yud'aw" with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the 'ayn followed by a waw, with "kull" in the nominative. This is explained in two ways. The apparent form is "yud'awna," with the nun present, which is the sign of the first nominative. The waw is not a pronoun of plurality nor its sign, but a letter of the word itself. It was originally an alif, and the original form is "yud'a," as in the other reading, but the alif was changed to a waw according to the dialect of those who say "af'uw" for "af'a," meaning serpent. This dialect is specific to pausal forms according to the well-known view, so here the connected reading is treated as if it were a pause. It is related from Sibawayh that changing a final alif to waw is a dialect in all cases. The second explanation is that the waw is a pronoun or a sign, as in "yata'aqabuna fikum mala'ikatun" (angels succeed one another among you), and the nun is deleted, as in the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "You will not believe until you love one another," and "as you are, so will you be ruled over." This is according to one view, and likewise in the verse of the poet:

"I spend the night travelling while you spend it rubbing your face with ambergris and fragrant musk."

It seems that because it is a sign of case, it is treated like its vowel, sometimes shown and sometimes implied. There is no difference, as a sign of case, between the waw being a pronoun or a sign of the plural, according to the correct view. The apparent view is that its deletion in the case mentioned is rare, not a necessity; otherwise this explanation would not be valid for the verse. As for the justification of the nominative "kull" in this reading, the views on the justification of the nominative in such cases are well known in the books of grammar.

﴿Then whoever is given his book﴾: on that Day, from among those called, ﴿his book﴾: the record of their deeds, and God, Exalted is He, knows its reality best. ﴿In his right hand﴾: to show the great value of the book given, to honour its owner, and to give him good news from the outset of what is within it. ﴿Those﴾: a demonstrative referring to "whoever" according to its meaning, as if it were indicated that they are a group gathered on a lofty matter. It was said: it implies that their reading of their books is done together, not individually, as in the case of receiving them. Most reports clearly indicate that the state of reading is like the state of receiving. Yes, a narration from 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, has come: "The servant is given his book in his right hand, and he reads his bad deeds while people read his good deeds. Then the page is turned, and God turns his good deeds so that people read them, and they say: 'This servant had no bad deed.'"

It is possible that everyone given his book in his right hand, after reading it alone, goes to his companions and says: ﴿Come, read my book!﴾ and they gather around him, read it, and he reads it with them too, delighting in it. But we have not found a report on this, and even so it does not achieve what the speaker intended. Adding the demonstrative with the sign of distance indicates the elevated rank of those indicated, that is: "those" who are singled out for that honour, which the giving of the book in the right hand suggests. ﴿They will read﴾ even if they were not readers in the world, ﴿their book﴾ which they were given in the right hand, so that they may recall their deeds and become aware of their details, and thus be held to account for them. It was said: they will read it boastfully, in what is inscribed in it of good deeds leading to various honours.

The use of the explicit noun in place of the pronoun is for greater emphasis. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: that is, they will not be diminished from the rewards of their deeds recorded in their books, rather they will be given them multiplied. ﴿Even a fatil﴾: that is, the amount of a fatil. A fatil is the thin membrane in the split of a date stone, named so because it resembles something twisted. It was also said: it is what you twist between your fingers of thread or dirt, and it is used as a proverb for something insignificant.

Now, what comes quickly to mind is that the agent of the giving are the angels, peace be upon them, who give the fortunate person his book, after it is called, in his right hand, so he reads it, is judged with an easy reckoning, and returns to his family rejoicing.

However, al-'Uqayli narrated from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The books are all under the Throne. When the Day of Resurrection comes, God, Exalted is He, sends a wind that scatters them to the right and the left, and the first line in them is: ﴿Read your book; today your own self is sufficient to take account of you﴾." This clearly indicates that the agent of giving is not the angel. However, the report needs examination, for I am not certain of its soundness.

Yes, a hadith has come which Imam Ahmad narrated: "From 'A'isha al-Siddiqah, may God be pleased with her, who said: 'I said: O Messenger of God, will a beloved remember his beloved on the Day of Resurrection? He said: As for three occasions, no — ...' and he said: 'and at the scattering of the books.'"

This supports, by its apparent meaning, the previous report. And God knows best.

It has been related in some reports that the first from this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand is Abu Salamah ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, and the first to be given his record in his left hand is his brother al-Aswad. God Most High will blacken his face after he extends his right hand to take it, and an angel will tear it away from him. The reason for this is mentioned in the books of biography (siyar).

[p. 123]

﴿And whoever﴾ is among those summoned and mentioned, ﴿in this﴾ world, in which such honour and favour were bestowed upon them, ﴿is blind﴾, not guided to the path of his salvation, which is to look upon what his Master, exalted is His majesty, has bestowed upon him, and to fulfil His rights and thank Him, glorified is He, in the manner befitting His exalted majesty, through faith and action. ﴿Then he, in the Hereafter﴾, which He expressed by: "the day We shall summon" ﴿is blind﴾, also not guided to what would save him, and does not attain what would benefit him, because the first blindness necessitates the second. In both places it is used metaphorically from the affliction of the eye.

It is also permissible that the second ﴿blind﴾ is an elative (af'al al-tafdil, the comparative/superlative form) of the blindness of insight, which is one of the inward defects from which the elative may be formed, such as "the most foolish" and "the most stupid." On this basis, Abu 'Amr inclines the first and emphasises (tafkhim) the second, and it shows that the alif in the first is the end of the word, as you see. Inclination (imala, pronouncing the vowel toward i) is good at word-endings, but in the second, on the assumption that it is an elative, it is as if it were in the middle of the word, because the mentioned af'al is not defined by the article (al-) nor in a construct, and is not used without the preposition min (than) governing the object of comparison, whether spoken or implied, and it is in the ruling of a single word together with it. Inclination is not good in it, nor is it common, as it is in the final position.

Abu 'Ali (al-Farisi) has declared this in al-Hujja (his book on the readings), so there is no objection to the inclination of "adna min dhalika" and "al-kafirin." Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr incline "al-a'ma" in both places, and there is no need to say that they do not regard it as an elative, or that the inclination in what they regard as such is for the sake of harmonisation (mushakala). Some of the verifiers (muhaqqiqun) said: since it was intended that the meaning of "blind" should differ in the two places, the two words diverged in inclination and emphasis. The second was emphasised because what indicates an increase in meaning is more deserving of emphasis, while inclination is less good in it than in the first. One should not suppose that Abu 'Ali holds the prohibition of inclination; he only holds that emphasis is preferable.

Some of them said: if blindness in what belongs to the eye and what belongs to insight is literal, there is no difficulty. If it is literal in the first and used figuratively for the second, there is a difficulty, unless it is said that it has been attached to what was set for it. Others have prohibited this, because the cause, which is the ambiguity through the description, is present in it. So reflect. This interpretation is strengthened by the conjunction of His words, exalted is He: ﴿and more misguided in the way﴾, in the world, because the capacity has departed and there is no possibility of making up what has been missed. This very thing is the one who is given his book in his left hand, by the indication of the state of the opposing group before him. Perhaps the shift to this designation is to signal the cause that necessitates it, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿But if he is of those who deny﴾, after His words, glorified is He: ﴿But if he is of the companions of the right﴾, and to allude to the cause of the state of the first group. In this there is what is of the kind of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one side mentions the effect and the other the cause, and each side's mention indicates the omitted element on the other side), relying on the testimony of reason.

Ibn al-Munayyir made it a counterpart to the first division, in the sense of: ﴿Then whoever is given his book in his right hand﴾ — he is the one who looks into it and reads it; and whoever was blind in the world, not perceiving his own self and not looking into his return, is likewise in the Hereafter, not perceiving his book, but blind to it, or more blind than he was in the world, according to the difference between the two interpretations. This, however, goes against the apparent meaning.

It also suggests that whoever was blind in the world to following the path of his salvation will not read his book in the Hereafter, which contradicts what is stated in the verses and the hadiths. Yes, there is a difference between the two readings, and perhaps the verse suggests the difference even if it does not establish the contrast as mentioned.

Furthermore, from Abu Muslim comes the interpretation of the second ﴿blind﴾ as blind of the eye, and this is not permissible. That is: whoever was blind of heart in the world will be blind of eye in the Hereafter, that is, he will be gathered thus as a punishment for his error in the world. This is like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾, the verse. And ﴿Your sight today is sharp﴾ he interpreted as knowledge and recognition. From him also comes the permissibility that blindness is an expression for the excessive distress that befalls him, as if it were said: whoever was astray in the world will be greatly grieved in the Hereafter, for whoever sees nothing but what displeases him is the same as the blind. This is like the saying: "So-and-so is hot-eyed (sakhin al-ayn, i.e., weeping, grieving)." And this, as you see, is weak.

It was also said: this is a reference to the blessings mentioned before, in the sense of: whoever was blind, not perceiving these blessings though he witnessed them, is in matters of the Hereafter, which he did not witness, blind and more misguided in the way. He relied in this on what al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from 'Ikrima, who said: some men from the people of Yemen came to Ibn 'Abbas, and one of them asked him: "Tell us about His words: ﴿And whoever is blind in this world, he will be blind in the Hereafter﴾." Ibn 'Abbas said: "You have not reached the point of the question; read what comes before it: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ships for you in the sea﴾ until ﴿and We have favoured them over many of those We created with a [marked] preference.﴾" Then he said: whoever was blind to these blessings which he has seen and witnessed, is in the matter of the Hereafter, which he has not seen nor witnessed, blind and more misguided in the way.

In another narration, transmitted from him by Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azama (The Greatness), through the route of al-Dahhak, he said regarding the verse: He, exalted is He, says: whoever was blind in the world to what he saw of My power, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the mountains, the seas, the people, the beasts and the like, then he is blind to what I have described to him in the Hereafter, and more misguided in the way. He, glorified is He, says: more remote in argument.

Abu al-Shaykh transmitted similarly from Qatada. It is not hidden that both interpretations are very far-fetched, though the second is less far-fetched than the first. I do not think the scholar (al-habr, the learned one, i.e., Ibn 'Abbas) would say that. And God, exalted is He, knows best.

* * *

"And among the allusive (ishara) readings of the verses" ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you shall not worship except Him﴾: The Wujudiyya among the Sufis (the adherents of the doctrine of the oneness of being, wahdat al-wujud) said: He, exalted is He, has decreed beforehand that none is worshipped but Him, so every worshipper only worships God, glorified is He, in so far as he knows and in so far as he does not know. For He, exalted is His majesty, is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and the fixed entities (al-a'yan al-thabita) never smelt the scent of existence, nor will they ever smell it. Among what they attribute to Zayn al-'Abidin, may God be pleased with him, and which they claim indicates their claim, is his saying:

"Indeed I conceal from my knowledge its jewels,
lest the one of ignorance sees the truth and is tempted by us.
Abu Hasan has preceded in this, to al-Husayn,
and he willed before him to al-Hasan.
For many a jewel, a sign, if I were to disclose it,
it would be said to me: 'You are one of those who worship the idol.'
And men who are Muslims would make lawful my blood,
seeing the vilest of what they do as good."

They said: he, may God be pleased with him, meant by this jewel which, if he were to divulge it, it would be said to him: "You are of those who worship the idol" — the knowledge of unity (ilm al-wahda), since from it one knows that the idol and others likewise are a manifestation of Him, exalted and high, and there is no other abode in the dwelling. What was transmitted recently from al-Hallaj has been mentioned, and the like of it is abundant from the Shaykh al-Akbar (Ibn 'Arabi), may his secret be sanctified, and from others, Arab and non-Arab. He, may God forgive him, has opened a door in this matter that cannot be closed until the command of God, mighty and majestic, comes. It seems he bequeathed to him that he should disclose and scatter those jewels among the small and the great, just as he bequeathed to the two Hasans that they should conceal what they knew of that. In some of his books, may his secret be sanctified, there is what is explicit that he was commanded (to do so). If that is correct, then he is excused. As for me, I see no excuse for one who follows his path in speech while differing from him in state, for this matter is too lofty to be attained by one drowning in desires, a captive of what is habitual, and a hostage of customs. And to God, exalted is He, belongs the excellence of him who said:

"The women of the tribe say: 'You hope to see
the beauties of Layla? Die of the disease of hopes.
How will you see Layla with an eye through which
you have seen others, and you have not purified it with tears?
You hope from her for talk, while the talk
of others has run through the holes of the ears.'"

And it is not hidden that according to the Sufi interpretation of this verse, His words, exalted is He: ﴿And to parents, kindness﴾ would not be included in what was decreed, since no one would allow them to say: "Every person is kind to his parents in so far as he knows and in so far as he does not." And it is understood from the words of some Sufis that this is an exhortation to kindness to the Shaykh also; accordingly it may be that the dual "parents" is like their saying: "The pen is one of the two tongues."

﴿And give the near of kin his right, and the needy, and the wayfarer﴾. It was said: "the near of kin" is an allusion to the spirit (ruh), because it was previously in nearness and witnessing, then descended wherever it descended. "The needy" is an allusion to the intellect (aql), because it is incapable of attaining knowledge of the reality of its Lord, glorified is He. "The wayfarer" is an allusion to the heart (qalb), because it turns in the paths of the journey (suluk) toward the King of kings. The right of the spirit is witnessing, of the intellect is reflection, and of the heart is remembrance. It was also said: the first is an allusion to the brethren of gnosis (ma'rifa) who have reached the lofty stations, and their right is the mention of what increases their establishment; the second is an allusion to the lovers whom the love of their Master has occupied, so that they seek nothing else, and their right is the mention of what increases their love; the third is an allusion to the travellers on the paths of seeking, who ride the swift mounts of resolve, and their right is the mention of what increases their desire and eases their hardship.

﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it with complete extension﴾. In this there is an allusion for the shaykhs as to how they should be with the disciples (murids); that is: he should not withhold from the disciple the spreading of the virtues of knowledge and the realities of nearness; and he should not mention anything that cannot be borne, lest he perish; rather, let him be between the two.

﴿And fulfil the covenant﴾ which was taken from you before the creation of the bodies, namely that you should single Him out and not associate anything with Him.

Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "Your Lord has covenants upon you, outward and inward. A covenant upon the secrets (asrar) that you should not witness other than Him, exalted is His majesty; a covenant upon the spirit that it should not leave the station of nearness; a covenant upon the heart that it should not part from fear; a covenant upon the self (nafs) that it should not leave any of the obligations; a covenant upon the limbs that they should cling to good manners and abandon transgressions."

﴿And give full measure when you measure﴾. It was said: in it is an allusion to the shaykhs likewise, that they should not diminish for the aspirants (mustaaddin) what their readiness requires of the heart's overflowings (fuyudat qalbiyya). And in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And weigh with the straight balance﴾ is an allusion to them that they should present the inward and outward actions of the disciples to the Shari'a, for it is the straight balance, and its two pans are prohibition and permissibility.

﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾, the verse. In it is an allusion to some of what is incumbent on the wayfarer of firmness, caution, and restraint from idle claims. ﴿The seven heavens glorify Him﴾, the verse. You have already learned what the Sufis hold concerning the glorification of things, that it is said: "However, none hears it except one who has attained nearness through supererogatory acts, or upon whom some of His lights have shone," like those who heard the glorification of the pebbles in the assembly of the master of the perfect ones (ﷺ). Glorification by state is something no Muslim denies. Some Sufis established it on the basis that every thing has a property that belongs to it and to no other. Just as it does not specify it over all else, it desires and seeks it when it is not present, and guards and loves it when it is present. So by manifesting its property, it declares God, exalted is He, free from partners; otherwise it would not be unique in it. Thus the tongue of its state says: "I make Him one as He made me one." And by seeking His perfection it declares Him free from attributes of deficiency, as if it said: "O Perfect One, perfect me." And by manifesting His perfection, it is as if it said: "The Perfect, the Perfecting, has perfected me," and so on by analogy. And then it is said: the heavens glorify Him through perfection, influence and lordship, and through His being every day in a matter, and the like; the earth through creativity, provision and mercy, and so on; and the angels through knowledge, power and being free of matter, according to the view that they are pure spirits. And so on.

[p. 124 — end of part 1]

**Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 17, verse 72 (part 2 of 2):**

﴿When you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier.﴾ (This is) from ignorance and blindness of the heart, so they do not perceive your holy reality and grasp of you only the human form. The reason this is specified to the time of reciting the Qur'an, although they are at every time the most ignorant of creation about him (ﷺ), is that at that time the radiance of the lights of the divine attributes becomes manifest upon him, peace be upon him. So if they are veiled at that time, they are at other times even more veiled, and more veiled still.

﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ from the natural veils and the bodily conditions, ﴿lest they understand it﴾. For the Qur'an is His speech, exalted is He, and it is one of His attributes. If they do not know His Prophet (ﷺ), they do not know Him, mighty and majestic is He. And if they do not know Him, glorified is He, they do not know His attributes, exalted is He, and so they do not know His speech, glorified is He. ﴿And in their ears deafness﴾, because the filth of attachments has settled in them, preventing them from hearing the recitation. This arises from their ignorance of His acts, exalted is He.

﴿And when you mention your Lord in the Qur'an alone, they turn back on their heels in aversion.﴾ This is because their desires are scattered and their concerns are divided in worshipping their various gods, so the oneness does not suit their inner beings.

﴿On the Day He calls you﴾ to rise from the graves, ﴿and you will respond with His praise﴾, praising Him, exalted is He, with the tongue of speech or with the tongue of state, since He has manifested life in you after death, and the like.

﴿And you will think that you remained﴾ in the graves or in the world ﴿only a little﴾, due to your being distracted from that time, or your deeming the world small in comparison to the Hereafter. ﴿Your Lord knows best about you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you, or if He wills, He will punish you.﴾ In this there is an indication that will follows knowledge: whoever He, glorified is He, knows to be fit for mercy, He, exalted is He, wills His mercy for him, so He has mercy on him; and whoever He, majestic and exalted is He, knows to be fit for punishment, He wills His punishment for him, so He punishes him. And there is no concealing what is in placing first the side of His will, which is mercy, from the strengthening of hope.

﴿Those whom they call upon﴾, i.e., those whom the disbelievers call upon and worship, ﴿seek the means of access to their Lord, [as to] which of them would be nearest﴾. That is: the nearest of them seeks the means of access to Allah, exalted is He; so how about those who are not nearest?

The means (wasilah) originally means the intermediary by which one seeks access and draws near to something, and here it is obedience, as has preceded. It has been said: it is His ancient generosity and His all-encompassing kindness, mighty and majestic is He. It has also been said: it is the intercession on the Day of Resurrection. And since the station of the means in this sense is specific to our Prophet (ﷺ), they have applied the term "means" to him, peace be upon him. Some Sufis (mystics) interpreted it in this sense here, saying: whoever is worshipped besides Allah, exalted is He, such as Jesus, Uzair, and the angels, peace be upon them, their means to Allah, exalted is He, is our Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, he, peace be upon him, is the means of all existing beings and the intermediary between them and Allah, exalted is He, in His overflowing of existence upon them, and likewise all that is poured upon them. The creatures most favoured through his mediation are the prophets, peace be upon them, for they are rays of his lights and reflections of his traces. He is the True Light and the Absolute Prophet, and he was a prophet while Adam was between water and clay. The prophets received from him from behind the veil of wombs and loins, and they appeared while he was concealed, like the appearance of stars at night. When the sun of absolute prophethood rose from the horizon of manifestation, they disappeared, and their rulings were abrogated, in the manner of the setting of the stars and the extinction of their lights and their brilliance at the rising of the sun from behind the veil, shedding its cloak.
**[p. 127]**

﴿And they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment.﴾ This is because of their knowledge of His beauty and majesty. Hope and fear are the two wings of one who flies towards the presence of holiness and the garden of intimacy, and whoever disables one of them is disabled from flying.

﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾, up to His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.﴾ In this there is an indication of the differing degrees of the Satan's power to mislead the children of Adam. Whoever among them has a weak capacity, he incites and belittles him with his voice, misguiding him with whispering and murmuring, indeed with a fleeting thought and a passing suggestion. Whoever has a strong capacity: if he is sincere, free from the taints of otherness or from the taints of the carnal attributes, he cannot mislead him. This is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them.﴾ If he is not sincere, then if he is immersed in sensory preoccupations and absorbed in worldly affairs, he (Satan) shares with him in his wealth and children, incites him to associate them with Allah, exalted is He, in love, embellishes for him enjoyment, multiplication, and boasting about them, promises him false hopes, and adorns for him empty aspirations. If he is not immersed but is aware of his enticements, he (Satan) brings against him his cavalry and infantry; that is, he schemes with all kinds of tricks, plots against him with various trials, and advises him that acquiring kinds of worldly goods and pleasures is among the interests of livelihood, and deceives him with his knowledge and drives him to self-admiration with it, and the like, until he misguides him with knowledge. And if he is not a scholar but is a worshipper and ascetic, he misguides him with promises and deceives him with the sight of his worship and the purification of the self.

﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾, the verse. It has been said: He honoured them, exalted is He, by creating their father Adam in the form of the All-Merciful, and made this a inheritance for them by the rule of inheritance, since the child is the secret of his father. And He preferred them over much of creation by bestowing upon them blessings that exceed counting. It is also permissible to say: their honouring is by spreading the tables of bounty for them and making all others parasites; and their preference, by what was mentioned in the honouring first. And there are other possibilities in it.

﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾, i.e., We will call them by attributing them to those whom they followed in the world, because their love for him is the most dominant among all their loves.

﴿So whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾, i.e., from the side of the intellect, which is the stronger of his two sides, ﴿those will read their record﴾ and receive the rewards of their deeds recorded in it, ﴿and they will not be wronged the least bit﴾, the smallest, most insignificant amount of that. ﴿And whoever was blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.﴾ That is, whoever was blind to guidance to the truth, he will be blind in the Hereafter as well, ﴿and more astray in way﴾, because earning there is nullified. And this one who is given his record in his left hand is from the side of the self, which is the weaker of his two sides; however, he expressed it with what was mentioned for what we have previously stated. And Allah, exalted is He, is the Guide to the straight path.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 17, verse 73:

Then, when He, Mighty and Majestic, had enumerated His blessings upon the children of Adam, and then mentioned their condition in the Hereafter and their division into two groups, the fortunate (su'ada') and the wretched (ashqiya'), He followed this with mention of some of the wicked deeds of some of the wretched in this world, namely deceit, trickery and confusion directed against the master of the people of felicity, the one whose infallibility (ʿișmah) is certain, ﷺ. In this there is an indication that they are included among those who were blind to guidance in this world, included in the first place. So the Exalted and Glorified said: ﴿And indeed, they almost tempted you﴾. It has been said: it was revealed concerning Thaqif. They said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We will not enter into your affair until you give us qualities by which we may boast over the Arabs: we shall not pay the tithe (ʿushr) nor be mustered (for jihad), we shall not bow in prayer, every interest (ribā) owed to us is ours, and every interest owed by us is waived, and that you allow us to enjoy (al-Lāt) for a year, and that you make our valley sacred as you made Makkah sacred. If the Arabs say: 'Why did you do that?' then say: 'Indeed God Most High commanded me.'" Al-Tha'labi narrated this from Ibn ʿAbbas, but did not mention a chain of transmission for it.

Al-ʿIraqi said concerning it: "We have not found it in the books of hadith." Al-Zamakhshari related it with an addition, and others related that they requested three qualities: not performing the talbiyah in prayer, breaking their idols with their own hands, and that they be allowed to enjoy (al-Lāt) for a year without worshipping it, but rather to take what is offered to it.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no good in a religion that has no bowing (rukūʿ) nor prostration (sujūd)." As for breaking your idols with your own hands, that is for you. As for the tyrant (al-Ṭāghiyah), al-Lāt, I will not allow you to enjoy it." The Messenger of God ﷺ stood up, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, said: "What is the matter with you? You have harmed the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, for he does not leave the idols in the land of the Arabs." They kept at him until God Most High revealed the verse.

Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Mardawayh and others transmitted from him, may God be pleased with him, that "Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Abu Jahl and men of Quraysh came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: 'Come, touch our gods and we will enter your religion with you.' The Messenger of God ﷺ was greatly distressed by separation from his people and loved their Islam, so he felt compassion for them, and God Most High revealed this verse, up to His words, Exalted be He: ﴿a helper﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted through al-Kalbi, from Badhan, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Jubayr ibn Nufayr that "Quraysh came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: 'If you have been sent to us, then drive away those who follow you from the dregs of the people and their clients, so that we may be your companions.' Then it was revealed."

It has also been said: they said to him, peace be upon him: "Make for us a sign of mercy be a sign of punishment, and a sign of punishment be a sign of mercy, so that we may believe in you." Then it was revealed.

There are other reports concerning this that differ, and some of them contain what cannot be correctly attributed to the Messenger ﷺ and hardly admits of interpretation, and this indicates fabrication. Tafsir does not depend on any of that.

Whatever the case, the plural pronoun refers to the disbelievers, who are either Thaqif or Quraysh. The particle ﴿in﴾ (إنْ) is the light form of the heavy one, its noun being an implied pronoun of matter (ḍamīr shaʾn), and the lam is the lam that distinguishes the light form from others. That is: the matter is that they nearly, in their assumption, made you fall into temptation, so that you turned ﴿away from that which We revealed to you﴾ of commands, prohibitions, promises and threats, ﴿to fabricate against Us other than it﴾, that you would invent against Us other than what We revealed to you, such as what Thaqif proposed to you of prohibiting, for example, the pilgrimage, or what Quraysh proposed of making a sign of mercy a sign of punishment and vice versa. It has been said: the meaning is that you would take the place of one who fabricates against Us, for if you followed their desires, or intended to do that on Our revelation, as you are Our messenger, you would be like one who fabricates.

﴿And then they would have taken you as a friend﴾, that is: had you done so, they would have taken you as a companion for themselves, and the intent is that there would be between you and them friendship and companionship, while they are enemies of God Most High. Their friendship necessitates severing one's allegiance to His guardianship, Mighty and Majestic, as it is said:

When your friend makes peace with one you oppose, he has become your enemy, and speech ends.

It has also been said: the word khalīl here is from khullah, meaning need, that is, they would have taken you as a poor one in need of them. But this is, as you see, far-fetched.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 17, verse 74:

﴿Had We not made you firm﴾: that is, had it not been for Our making you firm in what you were upon of the truth, through Our protection (ʿiṣmah) of you. ﴿you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾: from the inclination (rukūn), which is the least degree of leaning, and its origin is leaning toward a support (rukn). They mentioned that when it is used without qualification it applies to the slightest inclination. (شَيْئًا) is in the accusative as an adverbial of the verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning: had it not been for that, you would have come close to inclining toward them to a slight degree, owing to the strength of their deceptions and the severity of their scheming. But the protection (ʿiṣmah) overtook you and prevented you from coming near even the least of the least of inclination toward them, let alone inclination itself. This is explicit that he (ﷺ) did not intend to accede to them and was not close to doing so. By this, the view of one who claims that he (peace be upon him) did intend it, and that the revelation of the verse prevented him, is refuted. It seems that he was deceived by the apparent meanings of some reports explaining the occasion of revelation, such as the report of Ruzayq in the narration of Ibn Ishaq and those with him, from al-Hibr (the scholar). It is not hidden that in His saying, glorified is He, ﴿toward them﴾ rather than "to" their accession (ijābah), there is what strengthens the indication that he (peace be upon him) was far removed from accession in the furthest degrees. This meaning that has been mentioned for the verse is the apparent one that comes first to minds. Ibn al-Anbari held that the meaning is: they nearly reported about you that you had inclined toward them, and their action was attributed to him (peace be upon him) metaphorically and by extension, as when you say to a man: "You nearly killed yourself," meaning: the people nearly killed you because of what you did. This is among the riddles that need not be pursued.

The verse has been cited as evidence that protection (ʿiṣmah) comes through God's granting success (tawfīq) and His care.

Qatadah, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn Muṣarrif read تَرْكُنُ with a dammah on the kaf, the present tense of رَكَنَ with a fatḥah. According to the reading of the majority, it is the present tense of رَكِنَ with a kasrah on the kaf. It was also said that it may be with a fatḥah, and this was regarded as an instance of the overlap of the two dialects (tadākhul al-lughatayn).

﴿Idhan﴾ means: if you had come close to inclining toward them even slightly, ﴿We would have made you taste double the life﴾, meaning a doubled life. This is an adjective of an omitted noun, and the genitive construction is either in the sense of "in" or for association. That is, a doubled punishment in life. By "life" is meant the worldly life, because it is what comes first to mind when the word is used without qualification. The same applies to His words, ﴿and double the death﴾, meaning and a doubled punishment in death, which includes the punishment in the grave and after resurrection. Some verifying scholars preferred that the original sense be: from the outset, "We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death," with the genitive being of the lam type, and the indicator of the omitted "punishment" being ﴿We would have made you taste﴾. The meaning is: if you had come close to what we mentioned, We would surely double for you the punishment hastened for the sinners in the worldly life and the punishment deferred for them after death.

It has also been said: by "life" is meant the life of the Hereafter, and by "punishment of death" what occurs in the grave. The question of the genitive and the estimate remain as they are. The meaning: if you had come close, We would surely double for you the punishment of the grave and the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, which are stored up for the sinners. In this conditional statement there is great exaltation of the position of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and an alert that the closer one is, the greater the danger. That is because he was threatened with double punishment for merely approaching the slightest inclination, while inclination has been lifted from us as long as action does not confirm it. A similar parallel in some respect is what came concerning his wives, peace be upon him, in His words: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, her punishment will be doubled twice﴾. It has been mentioned, as a reason for doubling the recompense for the error of the eminent person, that his error becomes a cause for others to commit the same, and they take it as proof, so it is as if he had established that practice.

And it has come: "Whoever establishes a bad practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection."

Accordingly, the punishment of the eminent person is doubled many times over for his error. Affirming a single doubling does not negate multiple doublings. It has been said that "ḍiʿf" (doubling) is among the names of punishment, and they cited in support the verse:

For the killing of Malik, when he departed from me, I spend the night in a painful doubling.

Some have said that ḍiʿf is not, by lexical coinage, a name of punishment, but it is used to express punishment because punishment is so often described with it, as in His words: ﴿a doubled punishment﴾. It is claimed that this is what the poet meant, and Allah knows best. The lam in "la-adhaqnāka" and "la-attakhadhūka" is the lam of oath, as explicitly stated by al-Ḥūfī, and the past tense in both places stands in the position of the present tense indicated by the lam, and the nūn is as explicitly stated by Abū Ḥayyān, to which we referred earlier.

﴿Then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us﴾, one who would repel the punishment or lift it from you.

It is narrated from Qatāda that when the words of Him, the Exalted, ﴿And indeed they almost...﴾ were revealed, up to this point, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye."

It is fitting for the believer, when he recites this verse, to prostrate in humility at it, to reflect upon it, to feel awe and to increase in steadfastness in the religion of Allah, the Exalted, and to say what the Prophet (ﷺ) said.

[Page 130]

﴿And if they were almost﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, as related from Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah and others, ﴿to drive you out﴾, i.e., to unsettle you and make you light (to be removed) through their enmity and deceit, ﴿from the land﴾, i.e., the land in which you are, which is the land of Makkah, ﴿to expel you﴾

[Page 130 continues]

i.e., to bring about your departure ﴿from it﴾. This attempt to unsettle (the Prophet) was by what they did of confining him ﷺ in the mountain pass (shiʿb) and restricting him, peace and blessings be upon him. This occurred after the revelation of the verse, as in al-Bahr, and it became the cause of his ﷺ emigration (hijrah).

﴿And then they would not remain﴾, i.e., if they had unsettled you and you had left, they would not remain ﴿after you﴾, i.e., after you (departed). ʿAta ibn Rabah read it this way, and it was regarded as good that this is an exegesis (tafsir) and not a recitation (qiraʾah), since it contradicts the consonantal text of the Mushaf. They recited the following verse:

*The abodes were effaced after them, as though the palm-leaf weavers had spread mats between them.*

The people of the Hijaz, Abu Bakr and Abu ʿAmr read ﴿khalfaka﴾ without an alif. The meaning is one, and both wordings are, in origin, among the adverbs of place, so either may be used. Both are also used for time, and their being prefixed to concrete nouns is common, like qabla and baʿda, by omitting a governed noun indicated by what precedes it, i.e., ﴿they would not remain after your unsettling and your departure﴾. ﴿Except a little﴾, i.e., except for a little time. It is also permitted that the estimate be: except for a little staying, and the two meanings are close. The first estimate was preferred because the broadening, meaning placing the adjective in the position of the modified noun with adverbs, is more fitting. This is a threat to them of destroying them as a collective, as a group, after his ﷺ departure by a little, and it was realised by the destruction of some of them at Badr, especially since they were their chieftains and leaders. You know that the majority of a thing may be put in the place of its whole. The little time, according to what Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi, was eighteen months. It is also possible to explain the expulsion as coercion into departure, and the threat as destruction of each one of them; i.e., had they expelled you, they would have been totally uprooted, root and branch. But the first (consequence) did not occur, because coercion into departure is a direct action, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed as an emigrant by the command of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, so the consequent did not occur. This is the exegesis related from Mujahid, who said: Quraysh wanted that, but did not do it, because He, glory be to Him, willed to spare them and not uproot them, so that whoever among them and their descendants would accept Islam might be saved. So He permitted His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to emigrate, and he departed by His permission, not by the expulsion and subjugation of Quraysh. The expulsion in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a town, stronger in power than your town which expelled you﴾, is to be understood in the first sense, and likewise in the words of Waraqah: "Would that I were a young man when your people expel you."

His words, peace and blessings be upon him: "Will they expel me?"

So neither the verse nor the report (khabar) includes an affirmation of an expulsion that we deny here. As for the claim that this leads to a contradiction between this verse and the preceding verse, on the basis of interpreting the expulsion in it as causing the departure, because kada indicates approaching it and not its occurrence, while this verse indicates its occurrence, the answer is that the most the preceding verse indicates, on the first interpretation, is the nearness of the occurrence of the unsettling from them, so that they would cause his ﷺ departure through it, and that it had not yet occurred at the time of the revelation of the verse, not that it would never occur, so as to contradict its occurrence later.

Al-Zajjaj related that their unsettling was what they agreed upon in the Dar al-Nadwah, namely killing him ﷺ. By "the land" is meant the surface of the earth absolutely. Abu Hayyan said: what is meant is this world. It has been said: the pronoun in (kadu) and what follows it refers to the Jews.

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, and Ibn ʿAsakir related from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, who said: "The Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: If you are a prophet, go to al-Sham, for it is the land of the gathering and the land of the prophets. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted what they said and set out on the expedition of Tabuk, intending nothing but al-Sham. When he reached Tabuk, Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And if they were almost to unsettle you﴾ — to — ﴿a transfer﴾,

and He commanded him to return to Madinah, and said concerning it: 'Your living is in it, your dying is in it, and from it you will be raised.'"

In another narration: "They said: O Abu al-Qasim, al-Sham is a sacred land and it is the land of the prophets. If you went out to it, we would believe in you. We know that you fear the Romans. If you are a prophet, go out to it, for Allah, exalted is He, will protect you as He protected other prophets." So he, peace and blessings be upon him, went out because of their words, and encamped at Dhu al-Hulayfah and remained waiting for his companions, and then this verse was revealed."

[Page 131]

So he ﷺ returned. Then he, peace and blessings be upon him, killed the Banu Qurayzah from among them and expelled the Banu al-Nadir a little later. It has been objected that this report is weak, it is not found in any biography or book that can be relied upon, Dhu al-Hulayfah is not on the road from Madinah to al-Sham, and in any case the land would then mean Madinah. It has been said: the land of the Arabs. It seems that whoever holds that this verse is Madinan relies on the reports mentioned. Al-Khafaji has explicitly stated that this view is not acceptable. And Allah knows best.

ʿAta recited: ﴿lā yulabbathūna﴾ with a damma on the yaʾ and a fatha on the lam and the baʾ, with shaddah. Yaʿqub recited likewise, except that he kasrah'd the baʾ. Ubayy recited: ﴿wa-idhan lā yalbathū﴾ with the nun omitted, and likewise in the Mushaf of ʿAbd Allah. The justification for including and omitting the nun is that the grammarians counted among the conditions for the operation of idhan that it stands at the beginning of the sentence. On the reading with omission, the sentence is conjoined to ﴿they would unsettle you﴾, which is the predicate of kada, so the condition is broken, since it is then placed in the middle of the speech, the following clause being the predicate of kada and like what it is conjoined to. On the reading with the nun, the sentence is conjoined to the clause ﴿And if they were almost﴾, so the condition is realised, and conjunction does not harm this. Abu Hayyan explained the cancellation (of its effect) by saying that ﴿lā yalbathūna﴾ is the answer to an omitted oath; i.e., by Allah, if they unsettle you and you depart, they will not remain. Idhan has been placed between the implied oath and the verb, so it is cancelled. He then said: It is also possible that ﴿lā yalbathūna﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject indicated by the meaning, its estimate being: and they, then, will not remain; so idhan falls between the subject and its predicate, and therefore it is cancelled. Both explanations are not acceptable, as is not hidden.

Surah 17, verse 77: Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani)

﴿Sunnata man qad arsalna qablaka min rusulina﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive of the verbal noun (mas'dariyyah); that is, "We have ordained (sananna)" the custom (sunnah) of those ... etc. It means that We do not leave a community that drives out its Messenger from among them to remain after him except for a little while. So the custom (sunnah) belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is attributed to the Messengers, peace be upon them, because it was established for their sake. What confirms this is His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿and you will not find any alteration in Our custom﴾, where He attributed the custom to Himself, exalted is He. Al-Farra' said: "Sunnata" is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition; that is, "like the custom of"; so one does not stop at His, exalted is He, saying: (qalilan). The intended meaning is the comparison of his state, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the state of those before him, not the comparison of an individual with an individual of that type. Abu al-Baqa' allowed that it be a direct object of a deleted verb, meaning: "Follow the custom of ... etc.," as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿so follow their guidance﴾. The most fitting connection to what precedes is what precedes it; and it seems he considered the commands that follow, which is contrary to what most exegetes hold. "Tahwil" means change; that is, you will not find any alteration in what We have made into a habitual practice; that is, no one changes it.

The intended meaning of negating finding here, and in similar cases, is negating existence. The proof that no one exists who changes the habit of Allah, exalted is He, is clearer than the sun at midday. The Imam has a discussion on this point that is not free of investigation.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 17, verse 78 (part 1 of 3):

Then, after He, exalted is He, had mentioned the plotting of the disbelievers and consoled His Prophet, peace be upon him, with what consoled him, He commanded him to devote himself to his affair of worshipping his Lord, exalted is His majesty. And He promised him what all creation would envy him for. This includes guiding him to not occupy his heart with them. Or: after He, glorified is He, had presented the discourse on the divine matters, the Return, and the prophethoods, He commanded the most noble of the acts of worship after faith, which is the prayer (salah). So He, majestic and exalted, said: ﴿Establish the prayer﴾, i.e., the obligatory one, ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾, i.e., at its departure from the circle of midday. This is what is related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and his son, and from Ibn ʿAbbas in one narration, and from Anas, Abu Barzah al-Aslami, al-Hasan, al-Shaʿbi, ʿAta, and Mujahid. The Imamiyyah related it from Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, and from other people.

Ibn Jarir, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in his Musnad, Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Maʿrifah narrated from Abu Masʿud ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Jibril, peace be upon him, came to me at the decline of the sun when it passed the zenith, and he led me in the Zuhr prayer.'" It was also said that it refers to its setting, and this is what is related to us from ʿAli
Page 132
, may Allah ennoble his face.

Ibn Mardawayh, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and others narrated it from Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn al-Mundhir and others narrated it from Ibn Masʿud. It was also related from Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Nakhaʿi, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi, and al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah adopted this view, and he recited for Dhu al-Rummah:

Lamps that are not driven by the wandering ones, stars, nor by the revolving spheres.

The root of the letters d-l-k indicates movement from one place to another. Thus in the zawal (decline) there is a movement from the circle of midday to what lies next to it, and in the setting there is a movement from the circle of the horizon to what lies beneath it. Likewise in the well-known dalk (rubbing), there is the movement of the hand from one place to another. Indeed, every word whose first letters are dal and lam, regardless of its last letter, indicates this: such as dalaja with the jim, from al-dulja, which is travel by night; likewise dalaja with the bucket, when one walks with it from the well-head to the outlet; dalaḥa with the unpointed ḥa, when one walks heavily; dalaʿa with the unpointed ʿayn, when one puts out his tongue; dalafa with the fa, when one walks the gait of one who is shackled, and with the qaf, when one expels liquid from its place; and walaha, when his reason departs. In it there is a figurative movement to other than these. This meaning encompasses both of the previously mentioned meanings. And if it is said that the movement in the setting is more complete, because it is a movement from one place to another and from appearance to concealment, whereas in the zawal there is only the first, it is also said that dulūk is a derived verbal noun taken from the bare verbal noun, namely the well-known dalk, and this is more evident for the zawal, because whoever looks at the sun at that time rubs his eye. On this view, "at the decline of the sun" is a metaphor for the decline of its beholder. It may be supported, in preferring the first view along with what has preceded, that the first prayer the Prophet ﷺ prayed on the day of the Night Journey was the Zuhr, and it is established that Jibril, peace be upon him, began with it when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, learned the manner of prayer over two days. Al-Mubarrad said: the dulūk of the sun is from its zawal until its setting, so the command to establish the prayer at its dulūk is a command for two prayers, Zuhr and ʿAsr. On the other two views, it is a command for one prayer, Zuhr or ʿAsr. The lam is for time-specification, attached to aqim, and it has the meaning of "after," as in the saying of Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah lamenting his brother:

When we parted, it was as if I and Malik, because of our long togetherness, had not spent a single night together.

And from it: I wrote it to you for three nights gone from such-and-such a month. It may also have the meaning of "at." al-Wahidi said: it is for causation, because the entry of the time is the cause for the obligation of the prayer.

﴿Until the darkness of the night﴾, i.e., until the intensity of its darkness, as al-Raghib and others said, and this is the time of ʿIsha'.

Ibn al-Anbari in al-Waqf narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq said to him: "Tell me, what is al-ghasaq?" He said: "The entry of the night with its darkness." And he recited the verse of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma:

She kept giving with her hands while being heedless, until the darkness and the ghasaq had spread.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: the ghasaq of the night is the entry of its beginning. The poet said:

Indeed this night has become ghasaq, and I have complained of worry and sleeplessness.

According to him it is the time of Maghrib, and this was related from Mujahid. Its origin is from flowing: it is said ghasaqat al-ʿayn taghsiq when it pours forth water, as if the darkness is poured out over the world. It was also said: the intended meaning of ghasaq al-layl is what encompasses the times of Maghrib and ʿIsha', and it extends to Fajr, just as the intended meaning of dulūk al-shams is what encompasses the times of Zuhr and ʿAsr. Thus in the verse there is the inclusion of the end within what it limits, and with the addition of what follows it there is an allusion to the times of the five prayers. A group of the Shiʿa adopted this and used it as evidence that the time of Zuhr extends until the setting of the sun, and the time of Maghrib extends until midnight. This is one of the proofs for combining the prayers in a residence without an excuse, which they hold, and they presented it, from what al-ʿAyyashi narrated with his chain from ʿUbayd and Zurarah, from Abu ʿAbd Allah, that he said regarding this verse: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, prescribed four prayers, whose beginning time is from the zawal of the sun until midnight. Among them are two prayers whose beginning time is from the zawal of the sun until its setting, except that this one is before that one. And among them are two prayers whose beginning time is the setting of the sun until midnight, except that this one is before that one." This is the view preferred by al-Murtada al-Murtada on the times of prayer.

The view relied upon by the majority of the exegetes is that the dulūk of the sun is the time of Zuhr, and the ghasaq of the night is the time of ʿIsha', as is indicated by the addition of ghasaq and the non-sufficiency with "ila al-layl." The prepositional phrase is attached to aqim. Abu al-Baqa' permitted its attachment to a omitted element that stands as a circumstantial state of the prayer, i.e., "extended until the night," but the first is better. The intended meaning of establishing the prayer within these two times is not continuous performance, but rather the establishing of each prayer at the time appointed for it, by the explanation of Jibril, peace be upon him, which is established in the authentic narrations that none of the Pure Imams, who have witnessed it, has narrated, with their being accused of heresy and impurity of inner character. Just as the numbers of rak'at for each prayer are left to his explanation, peace and blessings be upon him. Perhaps the restriction to explaining the beginning and end of the prayer times, without separating them, is because a person during the times between them is awake, so some of them are connected to others, unlike the time of ʿIsha' and Fajr; for by occupying himself between them with sleep customarily, one is cut off from the other. For this reason the time of Fajr was set apart from the other times. Then, the Shiʿi who uses the verse as evidence does not complete his argument from it for the permissibility of combining Zuhr and ʿAsr, and Maghrib and ʿIsha', unless he adds to it some reports, for when those are not added to it, it is more fitting that it be cited as evidence for permitting the combining of all four together, not two and two. And the weakness of using it for this claim is not hidden; this is why Abu Jaʿfar among them did not accept it. Yes, what they adopted is supported by the apparent meanings of some authentic hadiths, such as the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, which is in Sahih Muslim: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed Zuhr and ʿAsr combined in Medina."

In another narration: "He ﷺ prayed eight together and seven together, without fear or travel."

Its interpretation has been disputed. Some interpreted it as: he combined due to the excuse of rain, and combining for this reason by advancing or delaying is the view of al-Shafiʿi in the old school, and advancing only in the new school, under the condition mentioned in their books. Malik restricted the permissibility of combining due to rain to Maghrib and ʿIsha'. This interpretation is well known from a group of the earlier great scholars, but it is weak, because in Sahih Muslim, from him as well: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined Zuhr and ʿAsr, and Maghrib and ʿIsha' in Medina, without fear and without rain." That the intended meaning is "nor heavy rain" is not accepted by one of fair judgment, and the anomaly is not granted. Others interpreted it as: it was during cloud cover, so the Prophet ﷺ prayed Zuhr, then the cloud cleared and it became apparent that the beginning time of ʿAsr had entered, so he prayed it. In this there is that, although there is a slight possibility in Zuhr and ʿAsr, there is no possibility in Maghrib and ʿIsha'. Others interpreted it as: peace and blessings be upon him delayed the first prayer to the end of its time and prayed it in it; when he finished from it, the time of the second entered, so he prayed it, and the picture became the picture of combining. In this there is that it contradicts the apparent meaning to an unacceptable degree. It is also refuted by what is authentically reported from ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaqiq, who said: "Ibn ʿAbbas addressed us one day after ʿAsr until the sun set and the stars appeared, and the people began saying: 'The prayer, the prayer!' A man from Banu Tamim came and kept on, without slackening or turning back: 'The prayer, the prayer!' Ibn ʿAbbas said: 'Are you teaching me the Sunnah, may you have no mother! I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combine Zuhr and ʿAsr, and Maghrib and ʿIsha'.' ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaqiq said: 'Something troubled my chest about that, so I came to Abu Hurayrah and asked him, and he confirmed his statement.'" Others said: it is to be understood as combining due to the excuse of illness or the like, from excuses that are of its meaning. This is the view of Imam Ahmad, and of al-Qadi Husayn among the Shafiʿis, and al-Khattabi, al-Mutawalli, and al-Ruyani among them chose it.

al-Nawawi said: this is the preferred interpretation. The view of a group of the imams is the permissibility of combining in a residence for need, for one who does not make it a habit. This is the view of Ibn Sirin and Ashhab, among the companions of Malik. al-Khattabi related it from al-Qaffal al-Shashi the Elder, among the companions of Imam al-Shafiʿi, and from Abu Ishaq al-Marwazi, and from a group of the people of hadith. Ibn al-Mundhir chose it, and it is supported by the apparent meaning of what is authentically reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and also narrated by Muslim: that when he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined Zuhr and ʿAsr, and Maghrib and ʿIsha' in Medina, without fear and without rain," he was asked: "Why did he do that?" He said: "He wished not to put any of his community in hardship," and hardship here means difficulty. He did not give a reason of illness or anything else.

From what we have mentioned it is known that the statement of al-Tirmidhi at the end of his book: "There is no hadith in my book on which the Ummah has unanimously agreed to abandon acting upon it, except the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas on combining in Medina without fear or rain, and the hadith of killing the wine-drinker on the fourth offense," arises from a lack of thorough investigation. Yes, what he said regarding the second hadith is correct, for they have explicitly stated that it is an abrogated hadith, whose abrogation consensus has established.

Ibn al-Humam said: the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas is in conflict with what is in Muslim from the hadith of the night of the halt (al-taʿrīs), that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no neglect in sleep; neglect is only in wakefulness, that one delays the prayer until the time of another prayer enters."

There is room for discussion on this matter.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 17, verse 78 (part 2 of 3):

The position of Imam Abu Hanifa is that it is not permissible to combine the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers within the time of one of them, nor the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers in the same way, in any circumstance, except at 'Arafat, where Zuhr and 'Asr are combined because of the rite of pilgrimage (nusuk), and except at Muzdalifah, where Maghrib and 'Isha' are combined for the same reason. He relied on what has been cited as evidence. The Sahihayn (Bukhari and Muslim), the Sunan of Abu Dawud and others contain material that does not support this restriction. You know that caution (ihtiyat) lies with what Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, held, since the cautious person does not move the prayer of Zuhr, for example, out of its certain time, on which there is no disagreement, into a time on which there is disagreement. Many scholars have stated explicitly that when conflict arises, the more cautious opinion is given precedence. The conflict of reports on this matter is not hidden from one who investigates it thoroughly.

Some have claimed that the prayer commanded to be established is the Maghrib prayer, and that the stated limit explains its beginning and end, with the end point excluded. From this they derived that its time extends until the disappearance of the twilight (shafaq). This is contrary to the position of Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, in his later (jadid) view, that the time ends by the passing of the amount of time needed for wudu', ghusl, tayammum, a light search, the removal of a gross impurity that covers the body, clothing and place, covering the nakedness, seeking the direction of the qibla, and the adhan and iqama. To these are added the remaining recommended acts of the prayer mentioned earlier, such as wearing a turban, putting on a shirt, walking to the place of congregation, a hungry person eating until satisfied, and seven rak'ahs. Perhaps the time that can accommodate all of this exceeds the time between sunset and the disappearance of the twilight, whichever twilight it is, in most cases.

Furthermore, it is not hidden that if what is meant by the darkness of the night (ghasaq al-layl) is the time of 'Isha', and ghasaq is interpreted as the gathering of darkness and its intensity, then this supports the apparent narration (zahir al-riwaya) from Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, that the beginning of the time of 'Isha' is when the twilight disappears, meaning the whiteness that follows the redness on the western horizon, because darkness does not gather and intensify until that has set. This is not contradicted by the sound hadiths, which are explicit that the beginning of its time is when the twilight (shafaq) disappears, and shafaq in linguistic usage means the known redness. This is because its interpretation as whiteness has also been reported. That interpretation is related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, Mu'adh ibn Jabal and 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with them all. 'Abd al-Razzaq related it from Abu Hurayra and from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, and it was the view of al-Awza'i, al-Muzani, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Khattabi. It was chosen by al-Mubarrad and Tha'lab. Also, what al-Tirmidhi related from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The beginning of the time of 'Isha' is when the horizon disappears" is apparent that the shafaq is whiteness, since the horizon cannot disappear except by its (the whiteness') falling away.

Yes, his two companions (Abu Yusuf and Muhammad) held that it is the redness, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them. Asad ibn 'Amr related it from the Imam as well, but this contradicts the apparent narration from him. The sound view on which we give fatwa is what appears in the zahir al-riwaya. This was explicitly stated by the scholar Ibn al-Humam, the 'allama Qasim, Ibn Nujaym and others. As for what Abu al-Mafakhir said, that the Imam returned to the view of his two companions and said that it is the redness, because it was established for him that the majority of the Companions understood it in that way, and that the fatwa is based on it, and al-Mahbubi and Sadr al-Shari'a followed him, this has no weight, because the retraction was never established. Without establishing it, against the transmission of the whole community from the whole community, the claim is like pulling out thorns from a thornbush (kharṭ al-qatad). Likewise the claim that the majority of the Companions understood it contrary to what has been transmitted, as you have heard.
